description.narrative: Sida's decision to contribute to the "Strengthening Democratic Resilience in Moldova" (EDMITE III) is based on the project's critical role in enhancing Moldova's democratic institutions and processes in a challenging political landscape. The key reasons for the decision include addressing threats such as cyber operations, information manipulation, and illicit political financing, which undermine Moldova's democratic processes. The project aligns with international standards like those of ODIHR and the Venice Commission, and aims to strengthen oversight, transparency, electoral institution resilience, and civic engagement. The funding will support the Central Electoral Commission (CEC) and other institutions in their efforts to improve electoral processes, manage political finance, and promote inclusive civic participation during the appraisal included Moldova's geopolitical vulnerability to internal and external threats, the need for regulatory improvements in political finance, and the enhancement of civic education to foster an engaged electorate. The project also focuses on gender inclusivity, cybersecurity, and the capacity-building of electoral bodies.

Sidas beslut att bidra till projektet ” Förstärkning av den demokratiska motståndskraften i Moldavien” (EDMITE III) baseras på projektets kritiska roll i att stärka Moldaviens demokratiska institutioner och processer i ett utmanande politiskt landskap. De viktigaste skälen till beslutet är att projektet ska hantera hot som cyberoperationer, informationsmanipulation och olaglig politisk finansiering, som undergräver Moldaviens demokratiska processer. Projektet är i linje med internationella standarder som ODIHR:s och Venedigkommissionens och syftar till att stärka tillsyn, transparens, valinstitutionernas motståndskraft och medborgarnas engagemang. Finansieringen kommer att stödja den centrala valkommissionen (CEC) och andra institutioner i deras ansträngningar att förbättra valprocesserna, hantera politisk finansiering och främja ett inkluderande medborgardeltagande under utvärderingen inkluderade Moldaviens geopolitiska sårbarhet för interna och externa hot, behovet av förbättringar av regleringen av politisk finansiering och förbättringen av medborgarutbildningen för att främja en engagerad väljarkår. Projektet fokuserar också på jämställdhet, cybersäkerhet och kapacitetsuppbyggnad av valorgan.

UNDP has requested funding from Sida for a new elections initiative project entitled "Strengthening Democratic Resilience in Moldova" (EDMITE III), which aims to bolster democratic consolidation in Moldova amid significant internal and external challenges, such as cyber operations and political financing issues. This initiative, developed in response to the 2024 UN Electoral Assistance Needs Assessment Mission, will run from August 2024 to December 2028 and focuses on enhancing oversight and transparency for political contestants, strengthening electoral institutions, and deepening civic engagement. The project is based on a theory of change that posits that improved oversight and transparency, strengthened electoral institutions, and enhanced civic engagement will collectively reinforce Moldova's democratic framework. It encompasses three key outputs: 1.Improved Oversight of Political Finance, Parties, and Campaigns: Enhancing the regulatory framework to combat illicit political financing and promote transparency. 2.Strengthened Electoral Institutions: Building the resilience and capacity of electoral institutions to protect against cyber and information threats. 3.Improved Civic Engagement and Inclusivity: Promoting inclusive participation and civic education to foster an informed electorate and increase women's political participation. Implementation will be collaborative, involving government, civil society, and international partners, and will be executed in three phases tailored to specific electoral events, allowing for continuous learning and adaptation. By the project's conclusion, EDMITE III aims to establish a robust political finance management framework, a legally fortified electoral system, and a more engaged electorate, ultimately reducing the vulnerabilities of Moldovas democratic processes and supporting its ongoing democratic development. Context: On 20 October 2024, Moldova will hold presidential elections and a constitutional referendum aimed at amending the Constitution to strengthen the countrys pro-European stance. This election is crucial as Moldova is at a pivotal moment in its journey towards EU accession, following the European Council's decision to open accession negotiations in December 2023. The elections will serve not only as a democratic exercise but also as an affirmation of Moldovas commitment to anti-corruption reforms and European integration. While Moldova has made significant progress toward EU membership, including the partial fulfillment of the European Commission's requirements, the upcoming elections will be a litmus test for the countrys democratic and institutional resilience. Ensuring fair, transparent, and efficient elections is crucial for maintaining international confidence and advancing Moldovas EU accession process. The project will focus on: Supporting the election administration, particularly in capacity building and ensuring transparency. Enhancing trust in the electoral process, especially addressing concerns raised about the CECs composition. Promoting voter education and engagement, emphasizing the importance of the constitutional referendum in solidifying Moldovas pro-European path. Given Moldovas strategic objectives and the importance of maintaining democratic standards, a comprehensive elections support project will be vital to ensuring the success and credibility of the 2024 presidential elections and referendum.

description.narrative:
Update of results: 2024
The Strengthening Democratic Resilience in Moldova (EDMITE III) project is a joint initiative supported by multiple donors and implemented by UNDP, with funding provided by Norway, Canada, Denmark, and Sweden. The project began in August 2024, and Swedens participation was formalized later, with the agreement entering into force on 7 November 2024. In this phase, the project not only launched its first set of activities but also ensured continuity by taking over certain uncovered activities from the previous EDMITE II phase, originally supported by USAID, thereby avoiding implementation gaps and ensuring smooth progression of reforms.
During the first reporting period of the Strengthening Democratic Resilience in Moldova (EDMITE III) project (August 2024March 2025), the initiative produced a wide range of results, many of them expected but some also emerging as unexpected outcomes.
Expected results were largely tied to the projects design:
- Political finance reform and oversight: The drafting and advancement of legislative package 381/24 was one of the most significant milestones, tightening the rules on political finance, introducing sanctions against electoral corruption, and addressing the problem of successor parties of banned political organizations. Alongside this, the project enhanced the Central Electoral Commissions (CEC) audit capacity, resolved more than 60 issues in the Financial Control Module (FCM), and supported systematic complaints management, including representation of CEC in courts. These steps directly strengthened institutional oversight of parties and campaigns.
- Institutional resilience and modernization: The project delivered urgently needed upgrades to the electoral IT infrastructure, including firewalls, penetration testing, and system adjustments for simultaneous elections. These measures ensured that, despite cyberattacks during the 2024 Presidential Elections and Constitutional Referendum, the CECs systems remained operational and transparent. The live results and turnout platform was upgraded successfully, while groundwork for the electronic ID (eID) system was laidexpected to significantly improve voter list accuracy and diaspora access to registration. Polling staff training was also expanded, with independent monitoring ensuring higher quality and preparing for certification standards to be introduced in 2025.
- Civic engagement and inclusivity: A nationwide campaignthe largest ever in Moldovareached over 2.4 million people through social media, Google ads, and mobile outreach. The use of I Voted stickers and wristbands for first-time voters boosted visibility and participation, particularly among youth. Teachers were trained to deliver a new civic education curriculum to secondary schools, embedding democratic literacy in the next generation. Campaigns highlighted womens political leadership, voter corruption penalties, and inclusivity measures. Partnerships with civil society advanced accessibility work in polling stations and raised awareness in communities vulnerable to electoral corruption.
Unexpected results also emerged, reflecting both the scale of activities and the political context:
- The reach of the civic education and voter awareness campaigns exceeded expectations, with evidence of strong public engagement online and offline. The creative use of youth-focused tools, such as wristbands and stickers, unexpectedly resonated with voters and created a sense of civic pride. - The institutional capacity of the CEC proved stronger than anticipated during the elections, as the rapid IT upgrades and technical support allowed it to withstand significant cyberattacks that could have undermined public trust. This demonstrated the resilience of the systems built under urgent timelines. - The public visibility of reforms, particularly the open discussions around cryptocurrency-based financing and third-party campaigning sparked broader debate in Moldovan society than initially foreseen, pulling in actors from law enforcement, civil society, and media. This cross-sectoral attention created momentum for reforms beyond the electoral sphere. - The legal defense of CEC decisions in court had an unexpected positive outcome: repeated dismissals of challenges to its rulings strengthened the Commissions credibility and signaled that judicial institutions were willing to uphold electoral integrity under close public scrutiny. While the expected results, such as legal reforms, digital upgrades, and civic engagement initiatives were achieved in line with the projects objectives, the unexpected outcomes showed the projects catalytic role in generating public debate, building institutional credibility, and fostering a sense of civic ownership among voters. Together, these achievements suggest that the project has not only addressed immediate vulnerabilities but has also begun to shift attitudes and practices in ways that could outlast the project period.
Update 2025: The 2025 implementation period of the EDMITE III project, coinciding with the parliamentary elections cycle, constituted a high-intensity delivery and validation phase for Moldovas electoral integrity and resilience architecture. Overall performance demonstrates full achievement of planned outputs under the projects theory of change, while also generating a set of significant emergent results linked to elevated electoral pressures, cyber threats, and evolving political finance and information risks. The combined evidence confirms both strengthened institutional capacity and real-world stress-testing of systems across electoral governance, digital infrastructure, enforcement mechanisms, and civic engagement.
From the perspective of political finance and electoral oversight (Output 1), expected results were achieved through substantial strengthening of regulatory and enforcement systems. The operationalisation of Law 100/2025 established an enhanced legal framework addressing illicit political financing, online political advertising, and successor party structures. The Financial Control Module reached full institutional uptake, with 100 percent of electoral contestants submitting financial reports through the system during the parliamentary elections, consolidating digital compliance as a standard practice. In parallel, the Central Electoral Commission demonstrated increased enforcement capacity, reflected in a significant rise in monitoring activities, administrative cases, and sanctions compared to previous electoral cycles. Capacity development activities further strengthened law enforcement and anti-corruption institutions, including training of over 1,500 police officers and targeted support on vote-buying investigations, illicit campaign financing, and emerging risks such as crypto-asset enabled political financing. The National Anti-Corruption Center benefited from enhanced investigative tools, contributing to improved detection and disruption capacity.
An important emergent result in this domain was the accelerated behavioural impact of the revised legal and institutional framework under operational election pressure. The combination of enhanced monitoring, civil society scrutiny, and media engagement contributed to greater deterrence of abusive practices. At the same time, the electoral process exposed persistent structural vulnerabilities, particularly in relation to cross-border illicit financing and coordinated inauthentic influence networks, which were more extensive than initially anticipated. Enforcement outcomes also indicated a growing gap between detection capacity and asset recovery mechanisms, especially in cases involving digital financial instruments.
Under electoral institutional resilience and digital infrastructure (Output 2), planned results were fully achieved and stress-tested under extreme operational conditions. The upgraded State Automated Information System for Elections (SAISE) and associated digital modules ensured uninterrupted election-day operations, including real-time voter turnout and results visualization, complaint management, and administrative support functions. The electoral platform served approximately half a million users during peak activity and maintained stability under high system load. Cybersecurity preparedness was significantly reinforced through system hardening and stress-testing measures.
A critical unplanned outcome was the unprecedented scale of cyberattacks targeting electoral infrastructure, with close to one billion attempted intrusions recorded and successfully mitigated without disruption to core electoral services. This event functioned as a real-world validation of Moldovas electoral cybersecurity architecture and demonstrated effective coordination between electoral institutions and national cyber defence structures. Additionally, the deployment and rapid adoption of the electoral complaints system and other digital tools under high-pressure conditions demonstrated higher-than-expected institutional readiness for digital governance systems.
Logistical readiness was also confirmed through the effective nationwide deployment of electoral materials and operational support systems, ensuring continuity of physical electoral processes alongside digital infrastructure.
In the area of civic engagement and inclusivity (Output 3), expected results were broadly achieved through large-scale voter education, outreach, and transparency initiatives. Civic engagement activities generated nearly 20 million online impressions and reached over 30,000 citizens through direct engagement formats. Targeted antivote buying campaigns reached over 22,000 citizens in high-risk districts, while structured civic education programmes engaged teachers, youth, librarians, and academic institutions. Civil society organisations contributed substantively to electoral monitoring and analytical outputs, reinforcing transparency and accountability in the electoral process.
Accessibility improvements were partially delivered through audits of nearly 2,000 polling stations and installation of selected accessibility infrastructure, although full compliance coverage remains incomplete. A significant emergent finding in this area relates to gender participation dynamics, where formal compliance with quota requirements coexisted with persistent underrepresentation of women in higher-ranked political positions and a decline in parliamentary representation compared to previous cycles. Analytical evidence further indicates increasing social resistance to womens political participation, particularly among younger demographic groups.
Across all outputs, several cross-cutting and systemic results were identified. First, the 2025 electoral cycle functioned as a de facto system-level validation of an integrated electoral resilience model combining electoral administration, cybersecurity, law enforcement, financial intelligence, and civic oversight. Second, enforcement and detection capacities developed more rapidly than corresponding asset recovery and financial seizure mechanisms, revealing an institutional bottleneck in addressing illicit financial flows. Third, the scale and sophistication of coordinated inauthentic behaviour and proxy media networks highlighted a more complex digital information manipulation environment than initially assumed, indicating regulatory and operational gaps in platform governance and digital campaign oversight.
In conclusion, the 2025 implementation cycle confirms that EDMITE III delivered all core planned results while simultaneously generating critical additional evidence on system resilience under stress conditions. The combined outcomes demonstrate strengthened electoral integrity, enhanced digital and institutional resilience, and improved enforcement capacity, while also exposing structural vulnerabilities in cyber defence scalability, cross-border illicit financing, information integrity, and gender equality in political participation.
A key political contextual result of the 2025 cycle is that the successful conduct and outcome of the parliamentary elections can be partially attributed to the cumulative effect of EDMITE III project interventions across electoral integrity, institutional resilience, and civic engagement. Strengthened political finance oversight, improved enforcement of electoral legislation, enhanced cybersecurity safeguards, and expanded voter awareness initiatives collectively reduced systemic vulnerabilities and reinforced public trust in the electoral process. In this sense, the 2025 parliamentary elections outcome reflects not only political competition, but also the stabilising effect of sustained technical assistance provided through the project over the implementation period.
